newsitem.title: UK: Britain slams Bosnia war crimes "snatch" report.
newsitem.headline: Britain slams Bosnia war crimes "snatch" report.

text.p: A British minister on Wednesday condemned a newspaper report that a series of "snatch operations" was being planned to abduct Bosnians wanted to face war crimes charges as "totally irresponsible journalism".
But Foreign Office minister Sir Nicholas Bonsor said he would not comment on whether the report, which appeared last week in the Daily Telegraph, was correct.

According to the Telegraph, the United States, Britain and France have been considering sending elite troops into Bosnia to pick up most of the 66 indicted war criminals still at large and send them to The Hague for trial.

It quoted what it described as a senior British source as saying: There have been intensive discussions on how to do it ...in the last month. There is a determination to do it, but still no final decision yet".
Bonsor, asked by a legislator about the report when he gave evidence to parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee, replied: "I think it would be extremely unhelpful for me to comment on that."
"The kind of alleged leak, or the kind of speculation based on alleged leaks, to which you refer are wholly against the national interest and, in my view, totally irresponsible journalism."
Bonsor said such reports were often designed to provoke ministers into commenting on policy which should be kept secret.
"It is the kind of journalism which we should all condemn. I am not going to comment on whether there is any truth in what the Telegraph has to say."

Bonsor said while SFOR, the 30,000-strong Stabilisation Force for Bosnia, would pick up alleged war criminals if it encountered them, the prime responsiblity for rounding them up lay with the governments of the countries into which the former Yugoslavia is now divided.

"At the same time, clearly in the event of their not carrying out those duties, we do look to see whether there are other things we could do to assist in the process of bringing these people to trial," he said.
